title: Biomass Organs Control the Porosity of Their Pyrolyzed Carbon

nodes.label: High-surface-area carbon for supercapacitors normally needs corrosive chemical activating agents added to the precursor
Why carbons pyrolysed from different organs of the same plant differ in porosity has not been examined
An organ's physiological role sets its native alkali load, which self-activates the carbon during pyrolysis, so stems should give more porous carbon than leaves
Lotus stem and leaf as a paired biomass precursor set from one plant

attrs.reason: the two organs differ in physiological role but share a genome and growth history

nodes.label: Organ (stem vs leaf) crossed with HCl washing and pyrolysis temperature 500-900 C, then repeated on celery and asparagus lettuce
Leach the freeze-dried organ in 1 M HCl before pyrolysis, so the organ architecture is kept while the metals are removed
Wash and freeze-dry the organs; the control set is additionally leached in 1 M HCl
Pyrolyse at 800 C under N2 for 3 h, then wash the product
The stem carries more total metal than the leaf and about 2.5 wt% K against 0.9 wt%
The carbons inherit the organ architecture, the stem carbon keeping an interconnected network of 5-30 um transport channels
S-carbon reaches 1610 m2/g against 1039 for L-carbon, with micropores near 0.9 nm and a mesopore population near 3.4 nm
After HCl leaching the two carbons converge at 909 and 803 m2/g and lose their mesopore population entirely
Potassium held at molecular dispersion inside the tissue activates the carbon in situ during pyrolysis, cutting both micropores and mesopores
S-carbon gives 174 F/g at 5 mV/s in 6 M KOH against 152 F/g for L-carbon
The S-carbon symmetric cell keeps 72% of its capacitance at 500 mV/s and shows no fading over 10 000 cycles at 1 A/g
The same stem-over-leaf porosity gap repeats in celery (1240 vs 330 m2/g) and asparagus lettuce (1075 vs 735 m2/g)
A plant organ's physiological ion load sets the porosity of its pyrolysed carbon, giving high-surface-area carbon with no added activating agent
ICP puts total metal at ~3.2 vs ~2.2 g/100g and K at ~2.5 vs ~0.9 g/100g for lotus stem against leaf

nodes.label: Across all three plants only K and the total metal are higher in the stem; Ca and Mg are always higher in the leaf, and Al and Fe only in celery and asparagus lettuce

attrs.image_note: judge re-read of the three ICP panels. Lotus F1e: Ca 0.72 (leaf) vs 0.50 (stem) and Mg 0.55 vs 0.21, but Na, Al, Fe and Cu are all HIGHER in the lotus stem. Celery F5d and asparagus lettuce F6d: every element except K (and Na, Cu, Zn in F6d) is higher in the leaf. So the leaf-over-stem inversion is consistent only for the alkaline earths Ca and Mg; the original 'Ca, Mg, Al and Fe in all three plants' was wrong for lotus. The audit's point stands: the paper's 'alkali or alkaline earth' framing of the activation holds only for the alkali.

nodes.label: Capacitance barely tracks surface area: 174 vs 152 F/g for a 55% area gap in lotus, and celery leaf carbon at ~330 m2/g still gives 132 F/g against 155 at 1240 m2/g

attrs.image_note: read by aligning the capacitance panels against the surface-area panels of the same species; over a four-fold area range the capacitance moves by about 15%

nodes.label: The stem-leaf capacitance gap could instead come from a difference in graphitisation or surface chemistry between the two carbons
The organ-to-porosity link is well supported, but the porosity-to-capacitance link is not: capacitance moves far less than surface area
2115 m2/g with no added activating agent is the highest reported for biomass carbonization and matches the high end of chemical activation
Alkalis naturally embedded in biomass activate the material during carbonization and create porosity in the carbon
Only part of the pore surface of a porous carbon is used for ion adsorption during charge and discharge
Stems carry water and salts up from the root while leaves make photosynthate, so the ion load should be higher in the stem
The best chemically activated carbons reach a comparable specific surface area

notes: The spine is a decoupling argument: the HCl-washed control branch (w6 -> w12) is what turns the organ/porosity correlation into the alkali-activation pathway w13, and x7 carries most of its weight because leaching removes the mesopore population outright. Two text-silent audits bear on the spine. a1: across all three species only K and the total metal are higher in the stem, while Ca, Mg, Al and Fe are consistently higher in the leaf, so the paper's 'alkali or alkaline earth' framing holds only for the alkali. a2: capacitance tracks surface area very weakly - 174 vs 152 F/g for a 55% area gap in lotus, and celery leaf carbon at ~330 m2/g still gives 132 F/g - which bounds the structure-to-property half of the argument (lim1). x9 records that the stem advantage peaks at 800 C and has largely closed by 900 C. Numbers are read from the panels: the celery 1100 C bar reads ~2115 m2/g against the ~2200 quoted in the text. Lost: the XPS panel, the supplementary time/temperature series S9-S10, the three-electrode data, and the micropore/total pore volume ratios quoted only in the text.

changes: a1: the audit generalised too far. F1e shows Al AND Fe higher in the lotus STEM, not the leaf (as do Na and Cu); only Ca and Mg invert in all three species. Label rewritten, image_support lowered shown -> partial, image_note now gives the per-species reading. The audit's conclusion - that the 'alkali or alkaline earth' framing holds only for the alkali - survives and is still carried by Ca and Mg.

x6, x7, x10, x14: provenance derived -> measured. Each reads a quantity the instrument or the paper reduced from data in the same panel (BET area, DFT pore-size distribution, specific capacitance), but none has an OBS parent in this graph, and v04 requires an incoming derives edge for derived. Each image_note now says which reduction is involved.

x7 and x9: attrs.text_silent removed. Both are primary evidence nodes with evidences edges into spine claims; the protocol reserves text_silent for content that earns a node of ITS OWN. Their text-silent observations are kept verbatim in image_note, which is what the rule prescribes. This also brings the audit ring from 7 to 5, at budget.

panel_checks.note: The three cited panels are the right ICP panels, but F1e does NOT show the claim as it was stated: in lotus, Al (0.044 vs 0.037) and Fe (0.019 vs 0.014) are higher in the STEM, and so are Na and Cu. Only Ca and Mg invert in all three species. No other panel would support the original claim, so there is no correct_id; the node has been corrected instead.

Exactly right, and it is the load-bearing panel of the paper. S-carbon peaks at ~0.9 (1.2 cm3 nm-1 g-1), ~1.6 (0.3) and ~3.4 nm (0.3); L-carbon at ~0.95 (0.65) with a weak ~3.3 nm hump (~0.09); WS and WL show only the ~0.85 nm peak and nothing above ~1.5 nm. Leaching does remove the mesopore population outright, and the caption never says so.

F5e gives CS 1240 m2/g and CL ~330 at 800 C; F5g gives CS ~157 F/g and CL ~132 at the lowest scan rate. A near four-fold area difference moves the capacitance by ~16%, which is what the audit claims. correlate_across_series is the right op and its correlational-only licence is respected.
Extra check. F5e: CS-carbon 1240 / 1225 / 1750 / 2115 m2/g at 800-1100 C, CL-carbon 330-570. The node's flag that the 1100 C bar reads ~2115 against the ~2200 quoted in the text is right.

review.audit_summary: After the two text_silent removals the audit ring is 5: x5 (rules_out against alt1), a1, a2, alt1 and lim1 - at budget. The division of labour is good. a2 and lim1 are the same finding at two levels and they bound the weakest half of the paper's argument: the organ-to-porosity link is well evidenced (x6, x7, x8, x9 plus the washed control branch), the porosity-to-capacitance link is not. alt1 is a properly stated alternative that x5 rules out with a real measurement (ID/IG 1.193 vs 1.174), not by assertion. a1 is a genuine text-silent contradiction of the paper's framing, now stated at the strength the panels support.
